cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO: functions and defects of form
cards.front: Which three forms (functions) of USUCAPIO does the textbook distinguish?
cards.old_front: Welche drei Formen (Funktionen) der USUCAPIO unterscheidet das Lehrbuch?
cards.back:
1. Usucaption for a defect of form: RES MANCIPI acquired without MANCIPATIO/IN IURE CESSIO → initially only bonitarian ownership.
2. Usucaption for a legal defect in the person of the transferor: derivative acquisition fails → the lawful possessor in good faith becomes owner once the period has elapsed (prevents a permanent separation of possession and ownership; in the meantime he is only a usucapient, not a bonitarian owner).
3. USUCAPIO PRO HEREDE: usucaption of (parts of) a dormant inheritance without SUI HEREDES — overt taking of possession + one year of undisturbed possession.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO: functions and defects of form
cards.front: What is USUCAPIO PRO HEREDE and why did it exist?
cards.old_front: Was ist die USUCAPIO PRO HEREDE und warum gab es sie?
cards.back:
Usucaption of items of the estate as long as there is no heir belonging to the household (SUI HEREDES) or the heir has not yet accepted the inheritance: overt taking of possession + one year of undisturbed possession.
• Reason: the ancient Roman cult of the dead — the heir was to accept quickly (and see to the funeral rites).
• An SC under Hadrian allows the heir to reverse its effect (Gai Inst 2.57).
• A detentor cannot usucapt PRO HEREDE (NEMO SIBI IPSE CAUSAM POSSESSIONIS MUTARE POTEST).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO: functions and defects of form
cards.front: In which two typical cases does a defect of form lead to usucaption (VIII.B)?
cards.old_front: In welchen zwei typischen Fällen führt ein Formmangel zur Ersitzung (VIII.B)?
cards.back:
1. OCCUPATIO of an ownerless RES MANCIPI: initially bonitarian ownership, after 1 year (movables) or 2 years (land) civil-law ownership.
2. Acquisition of a RES MANCIPI by mere TRADITIO from the owner/a person with authority of disposal ex iusta causa: initially bonitarian, later civil-law ownership.
• During the period the transferor keeps only a NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO: functions and defects of form
cards.front: Someone acquires a RES MANCIPI from an UNAUTHORISED person by TRADITIO — is he a bonitarian owner?
cards.old_front: Wer eine RES MANCIPI vom NICHTberechtigten durch TRADITIO erwirbt — ist er bonitarischer Eigentümer?
cards.back:
No — only a usucapient (if the requirements of VIII.C are met).
• Bonitarian ownership requires acquisition from a person with authority of disposal; then only the form is defective.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO: functions and defects of form
cards.front: Bonitarian owners are usucapients. Why is not every usucapient a bonitarian owner?
cards.old_front: Bonitarische Eigentümer sind Ersitzungsbesitzer. Warum ist nicht jeder Ersitzungsbesitzer bonitarischer Eigentümer?
cards.back:
Bonitarian ownership exists only where there is a mere defect of form (acquisition from an authorised person): the acquirer in substance has the strongest right, in content like a civil-law owner (ACTIO PUBLICIANA instead of REI VINDICATIO).
• Where there is a legal defect in the person of the transferor (unauthorised person, person lacking capacity), the interests of the true owner weigh more heavily → until the period has elapsed the acquirer is only a usucapient.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO: functions and defects of form
cards.front: What is the NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM?
cards.old_front: Was ist das NUDUM IUS QUIRITIUM?
cards.back: The “bare” civil-law ownership that remains with the transferor of a RES MANCIPI merely delivered by traditio during the usucaption period — a mere formality.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: What are the three case groups of legal defect in the person of the transferor?
cards.old_front: Welche drei Fallgruppen des Rechtsmangels in der Person des Veräußerers gibt es?
cards.back:
a. Transferor without ownership/authority of disposal → possession only (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
b. Acquisition from a PUPILLUS, FURIOSUS or PRODIGUS without the consent of the TUTOR/CURATOR → they are owners but lack capacity to dispose; no valid obligation-creating transaction → no IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS.
c. Person with full capacity, but no valid causa (e.g. dissent) → in some views a putative title suffices.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: If a PUPILLUS buys something without his tutor — does he have an IUSTA CAUSA for acquiring ownership?
cards.old_front: Kauft ein PUPILLUS ohne Tutor etwas — hat er eine IUSTA CAUSA für den Eigentumserwerb?
cards.back:
Yes — the part conferring rights on him is valid (NEGOTIUM CLAUDICANS); the contract of sale is a valid causa for his acquisition of ownership (cf. Marcianus D 41.1.11, Case 42).
• Conversely (the pupil alienates), there is no causa.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: What are the five requirements of USUCAPIO for a legal defect?
cards.old_front: Welche fünf Voraussetzungen hat die USUCAPIO bei Rechtsmangel?
cards.back:
1. RES HABILIS — thing capable of usucaption
2. TITULUS (IUSTA CAUSA)
3. BONA FIDES — good faith
4. POSSESSIO — (unflawed, uninterrupted) possession
5. TEMPUS — 1 year movables, 2 years land

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Which things cannot be usucapted (are not RES HABILIS)?
cards.old_front: Welche Sachen sind nicht ersitzbar (keine RES HABILIS)?
cards.back:
• RES EXTRA COMMERCIUM: RES PUBLICAE (e.g. market square), RES DIVINI IURIS (e.g. temple).
• RES FURTIVAE — stolen things (LEX ATINIA), for the thief and all later acquirers, in good or bad faith (Pomponius D 41.3.24 pr, Case 81).
• Things obtained by force, including land (LEGES IULIAE ET PLAUTIAE, 1st cent. BC).
• After REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM the stolen thing can be usucapted again.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: What is the IUSTA CAUSA USUCAPIONIS, what function does it have?
cards.old_front: Was ist die IUSTA CAUSA USUCAPIONIS, welche Funktion hat sie?
cards.back:
The usucapient's possession must be based on a title that would have given him ownership had he acquired from an authorised person — it corresponds to the IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS.
• Function: only someone who had good reasons to believe in his acquisition of ownership deserves usucaption; the title is the outward sign of this.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: In which two case groups do the Roman jurists largely dispense with an IUSTUS TITULUS?
cards.old_front: In welchen zwei Fallgruppen verzichten die römischen Juristen weitgehend auf einen IUSTUS TITULUS?
cards.back:
1. Acquisition from a PUPILLUS/FURIOSUS/PRODIGUS: good faith that one is contracting with a person of full capacity suffices — although strictly there is no valid causa.
2. Dissent between two persons with capacity: according to some jurists a putative title suffices, justified by BONA FIDES.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: What is a putative title — what is the Roman jurists' attitude to it?
cards.old_front: Was ist ein Putativtitel — wie stehen die römischen Juristen dazu?
cards.back:
A merely supposed legal ground for acquisition: the acquirer believes in good faith in a valid causa that does not exist.
Views:
1. Strictly rejected — a valid IUSTA CAUSA is necessary (Ulpian D 41.3.27, Case 91).
2. Rejected for sale, otherwise admitted — causa from the failed transaction (e.g. PRO DOTE) or a title of its own, PRO SUO.
3. Admitted even for a failed sale if the error is excusable (TOLERABILIS/PROBABILIS ERROR, e.g. deceived by slaves or a manager; Neratius D 41.10.5.1, Africanus D 41.4.11).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Why are the Roman jurists reluctant to accept a putative title?
cards.old_front: Warum sind die römischen Juristen beim Putativtitel zurückhaltend?
cards.back:
Only the VALIDITY of the causa can be dispensed with, not its existence: there must be reliable outward indications of an agreement on a causa.
• Only someone who had good reasons to believe that he acquired ownership upon receipt should usucapt — otherwise the owner's interests would be lost too easily.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: What is the content of the usucapient's BONA FIDES?
cards.old_front: Was ist der Inhalt der BONA FIDES des Ersitzenden?

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Language note: BONA FIDES, BONA FIDE, BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR — how are they used correctly?
cards.old_front: Sprachhinweis: BONA FIDES, BONA FIDE, BONAE FIDEI POSSESSOR — wie verwendet man das richtig?
cards.back: Whoever has BONA FIDES (nominative: good faith) is BONA FIDE (ablative of quality); whoever acquires possession in good faith becomes a BONAE FIDEI (genitive) POSSESSOR.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: When must BONA FIDES exist? What does MALA FIDES SUPERVENIENS NON NOCET mean?
cards.old_front: Wann muss BONA FIDES vorliegen? Was bedeutet MALA FIDES SUPERVENIENS NON NOCET?
cards.back:
Only at the time of acquisition.
• Later bad faith does not harm the usucaption.
• No room for BONA FIDES in usucaption for a mere defect of form; until Hadrian not in USUCAPIO PRO HEREDE either.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Controversy: does a usucapient who subsequently acquires bad faith continue to acquire the fruits?
cards.old_front: Kontroverse: Erwirbt ein Ersitzungsbesitzer, der nachträglich bösgläubig wird, weiter die Früchte?
cards.back:
Pomponius and Paulus: No — MALA FIDES SUPERVENIENS does not prevent usucaption of the fruit-bearing thing, but it does prevent the acquisition of fruits (Paulus (Pomponius) D 41.1.48.1, Case 103).
Julian: Yes — the effects of the initial good faith extend to usucaption AND acquisition of fruits until the owner sues (Iulianus D 22.1.25.2, Case 102).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Is someone who merely doubts the transferor's ownership, authority of disposal or capacity in bad faith?
cards.old_front: Ist bösgläubig, wer an Eigentum, Verfügungsbefugnis oder Geschäftsfähigkeit des Veräußerers bloß zweifelt?
cards.back:
No — MALA FIDES is only concrete knowledge of the defect; mere doubts still count as BONA FIDES.
• No duty to investigate the circumstances further (different in modern law: the error must not be based on negligence).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Paulus D 22.6.9.4 (Case 83): A (owner) sells and delivers to B; B wrongly believes he is acquiring from an unauthorised person. Does B become owner?
cards.old_front: Paulus D 22.6.9.4 (Case 83): A (Eigentümer) verkauft und übergibt an B; B glaubt irrig, von einem Nichtberechtigten zu erwerben. Wird B Eigentümer?
cards.back:
Yes — all requirements of derivative acquisition are met; B's mistaken belief is irrelevant.
• For usucaption B would be MALA FIDE — but that does not matter.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Paulus D 41.4.2.15 (Case 86): Purchase from a minor without a tutor. C wrongly believes D to be of age; E knows that F is a minor, but believes minors may dispose without a tutor. Who can usucapt?
cards.old_front: Paulus D 41.4.2.15 (Case 86): Kauf von einem Unmündigen ohne Tutor. C hält D irrig für mündig; E weiß, dass F unmündig ist, glaubt aber, Unmündige dürften ohne Tutor verfügen. Wer kann ersitzen?
cards.back:
Only C — he is mistaken about a fact (age) → BONA FIDES.
• E is mistaken about the law → a mistake of law does not establish good faith → no usucaption.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: Pomponius D 41.3.32.1 (Case 84): H buys a slave from the unauthorised G and (wrongly) believes that slaves cannot be usucapted. Can H usucapt?
cards.old_front: Pomponius D 41.3.32.1 (Case 84): H kauft vom Nichtberechtigten G einen Sklaven und hält Sklaven (irrig) für unersitzbar. Kann H ersitzen?
cards.back:
No — whoever categorically denies that the thing can be usucapted has no BONA FIDES; his error is a mistake of law and deserves no protection.
• (H presumably believes G to be the owner, so he is also mistaken about G's lack of authority.)

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: What requirements does USUCAPIO impose on possession (POSSESSIO)?
cards.old_front: Welche Anforderungen stellt die USUCAPIO an den Besitz (POSSESSIO)?
cards.back:
• It begins with the acquisition of possession; all other requirements must be met at that point.
• Acquired without flaw: not VI, CLAM, PRECARIO (IUSTA POSSESSIO) — Paulus D 41.2.5: whoever takes the purchased but not yet delivered thing on his own initiative cannot usucapt.
• Uninterrupted for the entire period; mediate possession through a detentor or a servant holding for the possessor suffices.
• Loss of possession ends the usucaption; on recovery it starts afresh — but only if he is then BONA FIDE.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: What can a usucapient do who loses possession during the period?
cards.old_front: Was kann ein Ersitzungsbesitzer tun, der während der Frist den Besitz verliert?
cards.back:
Reclaim possession with the ACTIO PUBLICIANA; in addition possessory interdicts, where applicable.
• The period starts afresh after recovery (good faith required at the time of recovery).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: How long is the usucaption period (TEMPUS) — and does the predecessor's period of possession count?
cards.old_front: Wie lang ist die Ersitzungsfrist (TEMPUS) — und zählt die Besitzzeit des Vormanns?
cards.back:
1 year for movables, 2 years for land; it begins with the acquisition of possession and starts afresh after loss of possession.
• Acquisition inter vivos: the predecessor's time does NOT count; only post-classical imperial rescripts allow ACCESSIO TEMPORIS.
• Heirs continue the usucaption begun by the deceased (SUCCESSIO IN POSSESSIONEM) — the heir's good faith is not required.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO for legal defects: case groups and requirements
cards.front: SUCCESSIO IN POSSESSIONEM vs ACCESSIO TEMPORIS — difference?
cards.old_front: SUCCESSIO IN POSSESSIONEM vs ACCESSIO TEMPORIS — Unterschied?
cards.back:
SUCCESSIO IN POSSESSIONEM: the heir continues and completes the deceased's usucaption; his own BONA FIDES is not necessary (classical law).
ACCESSIO TEMPORIS: counting the legal predecessor's period of possession on acquisition inter vivos — only through post-classical imperial rescripts; in classical law the acquirer starts afresh.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: What does the LEX ATINIA provide?
cards.old_front: Was bestimmt die LEX ATINIA?
cards.back:
Stolen things (RES FURTIVAE) cannot be usucapted until they have returned into the POTESTAS of their owner.
• Applies to the thief and all later acquirers, even those in good faith.
• Not to land (no FURTUM possible); for land, the LEGES IULIAE ET PLAUTIAE.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: What is REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM — when does it occur?
cards.old_front: Was ist die REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM — wann liegt sie vor?
cards.back:
Return of the stolen thing into the owner's power → the blemish of furtivity ceases, the thing can be usucapted again.
• In principle only when the owner again has IUSTA POSSESSIO: immediate physical control + knowledge that it is his thing.
• Not sufficient: return only to his manager (Neratius D 41.3.41, Case 73) or to the detentor from whom it was stolen (Paulus D 41.3.4.6, Case 72).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: Why is REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM framed so strictly?
cards.old_front: Warum ist die REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM so streng ausgestaltet?
cards.back:
To protect the owner: it would be intolerable if the victim of a theft also lost his ownership through usucaption by a third party in good faith.
• But once the thing has returned to him, his interest is satisfied; if it later comes, without theft, to an acquirer in good faith ex iusta causa, the latter can usucapt (REI VINDICATIO possible until the period has elapsed).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: What procedural constellation lies behind the cases on REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM?
cards.old_front: Welche Prozesskonstellation steht hinter den Fällen zur REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM?
cards.back:
A finds his lost thing with B and demands it back; B relies on completed usucaption.
• A must prove that the thing was stolen (RES FURTIVA) and therefore cannot be usucapted.
• B may nevertheless have usucapted if a REVERSIO to A took place before his acquisition.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: Paulus (Cassius) D 41.3.4.21 (Case 74): A pledges and delivers a thing to B and then steals it back from him. Can the thing be usucapted?
cards.old_front: Paulus (Cassius) D 41.3.4.21 (Case 74): A verpfändet und übergibt eine Sache an B und stiehlt sie ihm dann zurück. Ist die Sache ersitzbar?
cards.back: Yes (Paulus/Cassius): A is liable to B as a FUR (he took the pledge without B's permission), but the thing has thereby returned into the POTESTAS of the owner → it can be usucapted again.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: Labeo (Paulus) D 41.3.49 (Case 75): The pledger A steals the pledged thing from the pledgee B; later it returns to B. When does it become capable of usucaption?
cards.old_front: Labeo (Paulus) D 41.3.49 (Case 75): Der Verpfänder A stiehlt die verpfändete Sache dem Pfandgläubiger B; später kommt sie zu B zurück. Wann wird sie ersitzbar?
cards.back:
Only on its return to the pledgee B — the opposite solution to D 41.3.4.21.
• If the pledgee's right in rem weighs more heavily than the pledger's encumbered ownership, theft by the owner himself must exclude usucaption until the thing returns to the pledgee.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: Paulus D 41.3.4.13, 14 (Case 79): Apart from by return, when does a stolen thing lose its furtivity?
cards.old_front: Paulus D 41.3.4.13, 14 (Case 79): Wann verliert eine gestohlene Sache außer durch Rückkehr ihre Furtivität?
cards.back:
• When, through the REI VINDICATIO, the owner receives its monetary value instead of the thing.
• When it is transferred by the holder to another person with the owner's consent — the latter can then usucapt.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — LEX ATINIA and REVERSIO IN POTESTATEM
cards.front: Can a found thing be usucapted?
cards.old_front: Kann man eine gefundene Sache ersitzen?
cards.back:
Whoever finds and keeps a thing that has obviously been lost commits FURTUM → RES FURTIVA, cannot be usucapted; moreover the finder lacks title and good faith.
• Capable of usucaption only if it was really ownerless (abandoned) — but then acquisition by OCCUPATIO (for RES MANCIPI: initially only bonitarian).
• (Revision VIII question 8; answer derived from IV.A and VIII.)

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: What function does Roman USUCAPIO have — which modern institutions serve the same purpose?
cards.old_front: Welche Funktion hat die römische USUCAPIO — welche modernen Institute dienen demselben Zweck?
cards.back:
Protecting trust in honest dealings at the expense of existing ownership rights: once usucaption is complete, the usucapient acquires originally and the former owner loses his right.
• Modern law: usucaption and, above all, bona fide acquisition — immediate acquisition of ownership from an unauthorised person without any period.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: What are the requirements of bona fide acquisition in modern law (textbook VIII.E.1)?
cards.old_front: Welche Voraussetzungen hat der gutgläubige Erwerb im modernen Recht (Lehrbuch VIII.E.1)?
cards.back:
1. Movable things (immovables in Austria only via the land register, § 1500 ABGB, or usucaption).
2. Good faith: belief that one is acquiring from an authorised person; ignorance not negligent (in some systems only gross negligence is harmful, § 932 para 2 BGB; in some, belief in authority of disposal suffices, § 368 para 1 sentence 2 ABGB).
3. Unflawed possession (NEC VI NEC CLAM NEC PRECARIO) and usually a valid title.
4. In some systems, acquisition for consideration (§ 367 ABGB).
5. Significance in commercial dealings; acquisition from a person entrusted by the owner.
• Counterweight: public registers (ships, cars) exclude bona fide acquisition (Art 1156 Codice civile).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: § 367 ABGB: In which three cases does the possessor without notice of a movable thing acquire ownership from an unauthorised person?
cards.old_front: § 367 ABGB: In welchen drei Fällen erwirbt der redliche Besitzer einer beweglichen Sache Eigentum vom Nichtberechtigten?
cards.back:
On acquisition for consideration
1. in a public auction,
2. from a businessman in the ordinary course of his business,
3. from someone to whom the former owner had entrusted the thing.
• Requirement: legal (title) possession without notice. Claims for damages against the person entrusted remain unaffected. Para 2: third-party rights are extinguished, unless the acquirer was not without notice with regard to them.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: When is the possessor without notice under § 368 ABGB?
cards.old_front: Wann ist der Besitzer nach § 368 ABGB redlich?
cards.back:
If he neither knows nor has reason to suppose that the thing does not belong to the transferor; on acquisition from a businessman in the ordinary course of his business, good faith regarding authority of disposal suffices.
• Para 2: if he should have become suspicious because of the nature of the thing, a remarkably low price, known characteristics of the predecessor, the predecessor's business or other circumstances, he must surrender the thing.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: Roman USUCAPIO vs bona fide acquisition under § 367 ABGB — comparison?
cards.old_front: Römische USUCAPIO vs gutgläubiger Erwerb nach § 367 ABGB — Vergleich?
cards.back:
In common: good faith, unflawed possession, title (IUSTA CAUSA).
Differences:
• USUCAPIO needs a period (1/2 years); under § 367 acquisition is immediate.
• In Roman law a mistake of fact suffices, without any duty to investigate; the ABGB requires that one also had no reason to suspect anything.
• § 367 applies only to acquisition for consideration and in three case groups (auction, businessman, person entrusted).
• Stolen things: in Roman law never capable of usucaption (LEX ATINIA); under § 367 cases 1 and 2 stolen things can also be acquired.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: Is bona fide acquisition of stolen things possible under Austrian law?
cards.old_front: Ist nach österreichischem Recht gutgläubiger Erwerb gestohlener Sachen möglich?
cards.back:
Yes — in the first two cases of § 367 ABGB (public auction, businessman in the ordinary course of his business).
• Not in the 3rd case (person entrusted), because there the thing must have been entrusted, not lost against the owner's will.
• In Austria stolen things are not excluded from usucaption either.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: How do the BGB, ZGB and Code civil take up the idea of the LEX ATINIA?
cards.old_front: Wie nehmen BGB, ZGB und Code civil den Gedanken der LEX ATINIA auf?
cards.back:
BGB § 935 para 1: no bona fide acquisition of things that are stolen, lost or otherwise missing — exception in para 2: money, bearer bonds, public auction.
ZGB Art 934: things that have gone missing can be reclaimed for 5 years; if bought at an auction, at a market or from a dealer, only against reimbursement of the price.
Code civil Art 2276: “En fait de meubles, la possession vaut titre” — but lost/stolen things can be reclaimed for 3 years; Art 2277: if bought at a trade fair, market, auction or from a dealer, only against reimbursement of the price.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: Why does modern law in some cases allow persons in good faith to acquire stolen things?
cards.old_front: Warum erlaubt modernes Recht teilweise den Erwerb gestohlener Sachen durch Gutgläubige?
cards.back:
Because of the needs of commercial dealings: lean forms, quick processes, no researching of distribution chains, no risk of eviction, no period of limbo as with usucaption.
• Hence privileges for markets, trade fairs, dealers, public auctions, money and bearer bonds.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: Why do some legal systems privilege bona fide acquisition for consideration?
cards.old_front: Warum privilegieren manche Rechtsordnungen den entgeltlichen gutgläubigen Erwerb?
cards.back:
Because a person in good faith who receives something as a gift deserves less protection than the owner (A gives B a thing belonging to C).
• § 367 ABGB and Anglo-American law (BONA FIDE PURCHASER FOR VALUE) require consideration; the BGB, ZGB, Code civil and Codice civile do not.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: Bona fide acquisition under § 932 BGB and Art 714 para 2 / 933 ZGB — core statement?
cards.old_front: Gutgläubiger Erwerb nach § 932 BGB und Art 714 Abs 2 / 933 ZGB — Kernaussage?
cards.back:
§ 932 BGB: on a disposal under § 929 the acquirer becomes owner even if the thing does not belong to the transferor — unless he is in bad faith (he knows it or is unaware of it through gross negligence).
Art 714 para 2 ZGB: whoever in good faith receives a movable thing as owner becomes its owner as soon as his possession is protected under the rules on possession; Art 933: even if it had merely been entrusted to the transferor.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: What does Art 1153 Codice civile provide on bona fide acquisition?
cards.old_front: Was bestimmt Art 1153 Codice civile zum gutgläubigen Erwerb?
cards.back:
Whoever acquires movables from a non-owner becomes owner through possession if he is in good faith at the time of delivery and there is a title suitable for transferring ownership; acquisition is free of encumbrances, unless third-party rights appear from the title. Also applies to usufruct and pledge.
• Art 1156: not for aggregates of things and registered movables.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — USUCAPIO and bona fide acquisition in modern law
cards.front: Proper (short) vs improper (long) usucaption under the ABGB?
cards.old_front: Eigentliche (kurze) vs uneigentliche (lange) Ersitzung im ABGB?
cards.back:
Short (§ 1466 ABGB): movables after 3 years of qualified possession — legal (title), without notice, and without defect.
Long: even without a valid title, with possession without notice and without defect, after 30 years; good faith throughout the entire period; also for immovables.
• Usucaption of immovables is a departure from the principle of entry in the land register (§ 4 GBG).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Textbook exercises (Ex 29–34)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 29] Kassandra gives Cleo her horse as a gift. Two days later Xerxes steals it from Cleo and sells and delivers it to Thisbe, who is in good faith. Can Cleo get the horse back from Thisbe?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 29] Kassandra schenkt Cleo ihr Pferd. Zwei Tage später stiehlt Xerxes es Cleo und verkauft und übergibt es an die gutgläubige Thisbe. Kann Cleo das Pferd von Thisbe zurückbekommen?
cards.back:
Yes — with the REI VINDICATIO, as long as the horse exists.
• Cleo became owner: gift = IUSTA CAUSA, delivery by the owner. (Horse = RES MANCIPI: without MANCIPATIO she would be a bonitarian owner → ACTIO PUBLICIANA.)
• Xerxes could not transfer ownership (NEMO PLUS IURIS …); Thisbe cannot usucapt despite good faith and a sale — RES FURTIVA (LEX ATINIA).
• Against Xerxes additionally ACTIO FURTI + CONDICTIO FURTIVA (the condictio is not cumulative with the vindication).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Textbook exercises (Ex 29–34)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 30] Helena sells a horse, which Kassandra had given her for safekeeping and which she believes in good faith to be her own, to Leo, a slave of Japyx with a PECULIUM. Leo uses it for three months in the peculium and then hands it over to Japyx. After another ten months Kassandra demands it back from Japyx. May Japyx keep it?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 30] Helena verkauft ein Pferd, das ihr Kassandra zur Verwahrung gegeben hatte und das sie gutgläubig für ihr eigenes hält, an Leo, Sklave des Japyx mit PECULIUM. Leo nutzt es drei Monate im Peculium und übergibt es dann Japyx. Nach weiteren zehn Monaten verlangt Kassandra es von Japyx zurück. Darf Japyx es behalten?
cards.back:
Yes — Japyx has usucapted it after 13 months (movables: 1 year).
• No derivative acquisition: Helena was neither owner nor had authority of disposal.
• RES HABILIS: not stolen — Helena sold in good faith, without intent to enrich herself → no FURTUM.
• TITULUS: sale. BONA FIDES: Japyx/Leo believed Helena to be the owner (mistake of fact).
• POSSESSIO: Japyx acquired possession already upon delivery to Leo (PECULIUM, ANIMO SERVORUM); passing it on to Japyx interrupts nothing → 13 months uninterrupted.
• (Horse = RES MANCIPI; where there is a legal defect this is irrelevant — usucaption confers civil-law ownership.)

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Textbook exercises (Ex 29–34)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 31] Ago occupies a piece of land in the Alban Hills which he believes to be ownerless; it belongs to Bellona, who has not looked after it for two years. On 1 January Ago sells it to Cara; only on 15 July does Cara's slave Dexter take over the land from Ago and cultivate it. In the spring of the year after next Bellona demands its return. Is Cara owner?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 31] Ago besetzt ein Grundstück in den Albanerbergen, das er für herrenlos hält; es gehört Bellona, die sich seit zwei Jahren nicht darum kümmert. Am 1.1. verkauft Ago es an Cara; erst am 15.7. übernimmt Caras Sklave Dexter das Grundstück von Ago und bebaut es. Im Frühjahr des übernächsten Jahres verlangt Bellona es heraus. Ist Cara Eigentümerin?
cards.back:
No, not yet.
• Bellona's lack of interest is not dereliction; she remains owner (solo animo) → Ago did not acquire by OCCUPATIO, nor could he transfer ownership (NEMO PLUS IURIS …).
• Usucaption by Cara: RES HABILIS (land, no FURTUM possible; not seized by force), title sale, BONA FIDES (no knowledge), possession only from 15 July (taking over by Dexter — ANIMO NOSTRO CORPORE ALIENO; the sale on 1 January did not confer possession).
• TEMPUS: land 2 years from 15 July → not yet elapsed in the spring of the year after next → Bellona can vindicate (by asserting her claim in court).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Textbook exercises (Ex 29–34)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 32a] Flora buys a parrot from its insane owner Eros and receives it. After a year the parrot comes into the possession of Gripus. What can Flora do against Gripus — and does it matter whether she thought Eros was of sound mind?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 32a] Flora kauft vom geisteskranken Eigentümer Eros einen Papagei und erhält ihn. Nach einem Jahr gerät der Papagei in den Besitz des Gripus. Was kann Flora gegen Gripus unternehmen — und spielt es eine Rolle, ob sie Eros für geistig gesund hielt?
cards.back:
No derivative acquisition: the FURIOSUS cannot dispose, the sale is not a valid causa.
• If Flora thought Eros was sane (mistake of fact): BONA FIDES; on acquisition from FURIOSI good faith suffices instead of a valid title; RES HABILIS (neither stolen nor RES DIVINI IURIS/PUBLICA); 1 year of uninterrupted possession → Flora became owner by USUCAPIO → REI VINDICATIO against Gripus.
• If she knew of the insanity: MALA FIDES → no usucaption, Eros remains owner; Flora also has no ACTIO PUBLICIANA (she is not a usucapient), at most possessory interdicts if Gripus's possession is flawed in relation to her.

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Textbook exercises (Ex 29–34)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 32b] Flora buys a parrot from the insane Eros; she knows of the insanity but believes FURIOSI can conclude transactions to their advantage. Can she usucapt?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 32b] Flora kauft vom geisteskranken Eros einen Papagei; sie kennt die Geisteskrankheit, glaubt aber, FURIOSI könnten Geschäfte zu ihrem Vorteil schließen. Kann sie ersitzen?
cards.back:
No — that is a mistake of law; a mistake of law does not establish BONA FIDES (cf. Paulus D 41.4.2.15, Case 86).
• Moreover FURIOSI lack capacity to act altogether (they are not merely limited like PUPILLI).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Textbook exercises (Ex 29–34)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 33] Melitta borrows a handmade gold chain from Irene and, pressed by creditors, sells and delivers it to Pius. At the time of delivery Pius believes Melitta to be the owner; three days later he learns the truth. After three years Irene discovers the chain at Pius's. Who owns it?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 33] Melitta leiht sich von Irene eine handgefertigte Goldkette und verkauft und übergibt sie, von Gläubigern bedrängt, an Pius. Pius hält Melitta bei der Übergabe für die Eigentümerin; drei Tage später erfährt er die Wahrheit. Nach drei Jahren entdeckt Irene die Kette bei Pius. Wem gehört sie?
cards.back:
Irene — Pius could not usucapt because the chain is a RES FURTIVA.
• Melitta committed FURTUM (embezzlement: sale of an entrusted thing with intent to enrich herself, cf. Example 8) → LEX ATINIA.
• His later bad faith did not harm (MALA FIDES SUPERVENIENS NON NOCET), and title and time would be met — it fails solely on RES HABILIS.
• Irene: REI VINDICATIO against Pius.
• In modern law (§ 367 para 1 case 3 ABGB) Pius, as an acquirer for consideration without notice from the person entrusted, would have acquired ownership immediately.
• (The book once mistakenly calls the lender Orion.)

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Textbook exercises (Ex 29–34)
cards.front: [Textbook Ex 34] Nike buys a mineral collection at market price from 12-year-old Ramses (father dead, looks older; Nike thinks he is 15) and gives it to Leander, who knows nothing of the acquisition from Ramses. After 14 months Ramses' tutor, who had not consented, demands the collection back. Who owns it?
cards.old_front: [Lehrbuch Ex 34] Nike kauft vom 12-jährigen Ramses (Vater tot, sieht älter aus; Nike hält ihn für 15) zum Marktpreis eine Mineraliensammlung und schenkt sie Leander, der vom Erwerb von Ramses nichts weiß. Nach 14 Monaten verlangt Ramses' Tutor, der nicht zugestimmt hatte, die Sammlung heraus. Wem gehört sie?
cards.back:
What matters is Leander's own usucaption — Nike's period of possession does not count.
• No derivative acquisition: a PUPILLUS without AUCTORITAS TUTORIS cannot dispose (NEGOTIUM CLAUDICANS → no valid causa); Nike does not become owner and so cannot give Leander ownership either.
• But Nike was a usucapient in good faith: mistake of fact about the age (Paulus D 41.4.2.15); no FURTUM → RES HABILIS.
• Leander: title gift, BONA FIDES → he begins his OWN usucaption; inter vivos the predecessor's period of possession is not counted (ACCESSIO TEMPORIS only post-classical).
• The 14 months run from Nike's purchase: if Leander has already possessed the collection for ≥ 1 year (gift within 2 months of the purchase), he is owner; otherwise it still belongs to Ramses (REI VINDICATIO by the tutor).
• Against Ramses, Nike would at most have an enrichment claim for the price paid (cf. D 26.8.5 pr).

cards.topic: 03.11. Acquiring ownership II — Exam case MP June 2023
cards.front: [MP June 2023 · Case 2 (16 pts)] At the market Helena buys a silver brooch from eleven-year-old Gaius; she notices that he looks much younger than the other traders, but does not ask. Money and goods are exchanged immediately. Eight months later Helena dies; her niece Julia, who knows Gaius' family and knows his age, inherits everything including the brooch. After another five months Gaius' tutor demands the brooch back. Legal position?
cards.old_front: [MP Juni 2023 · Fall 2 (16 P.)] Helena kauft am Markt vom elfjährigen Gaius eine Silberbrosche; sie bemerkt, dass er viel jünger aussieht als die anderen Händler, fragt aber nicht nach. Geld und Ware werden sofort getauscht. Acht Monate später stirbt Helena; ihre Nichte Julia, die Gaius' Familie kennt und sein Alter weiß, erbt alles samt Brosche. Nach weiteren fünf Monaten verlangt Gaius' Tutor die Brosche zurück. Rechtslage?
cards.back:
Julia has become owner by USUCAPIO — the tutor does not succeed (if Helena's BONA FIDES is affirmed).
• No derivative acquisition: Gaius is a PUPILLUS (7–14) and disposes without AUCTORITAS TUTORIS → only NEGOTIUM CLAUDICANS, no IUSTA CAUSA TRADITIONIS.
• Usucaption: RES HABILIS (brooch not stolen; RES NEC MANCIPI); title: on acquisition from PUPILLI good faith as to capacity suffices.
• Helena's BONA FIDES (required only at the time of acquisition): she had doubts at most, but no concrete knowledge; mere doubts do not harm, no duty to investigate → in good faith (counter-argument: obviously a child; in modern law this would be negligent).
• Tempus 1 year: 8 months Helena + 5 months Julia = 13 months. As heir Julia continues the usucaption (SUCCESSIO IN POSSESSIONEM); her own knowledge (MALA FIDES) does not harm.
• Result: Gaius no longer has a REI VINDICATIO.
• (Source: studocu exam; solution according to textbook VIII.C.)
